phases: 1. Preparation: Pneumoperitoneum creation, trocar placement, camera insertion, initial diagnostic sweep, and cephalad retraction of the gallbladder fundus over the liver edge.

2. Calot's (Hepatocystic) Triangle Dissection: Incision of visceral peritoneum over Hartmann's pouch, blunt and electrocautery clearance of fibrofatty tissue to isolate the cystic duct and cystic artery, culminating in the Critical View of Safety (CVS).
3. Clipping and Cutting: Placement of titanium or polymer clips across the isolated cystic duct and cystic artery, followed by division with laparoscopic scissors.
4. Gallbladder Dissection: Retrograde electrocautery dissection of the gallbladder off the cystic plate (liver bed) from infundibulum toward fundus.
5. Gallbladder Packaging: Insertion of an endoscopic retrieval bag and placement of the resected gallbladder specimen inside it.

6. Cleaning and Coagulation: Irrigation and suctioning of the subhepatic space/Morrison's pouch, inspection of the liver bed and clipped stumps for bile leaks or bleeding, and electrocautery hemostasis.
7. Gallbladder Retraction: Extraction of the retrieval bag via the port, trocar removal under vision, and desufflation.

structures.name: Laparoscopic Grasper
structures.appearance: Long cylindrical shaft (5 mm diameter) covered in matte black or dark-grey insulation, ending in a metallic silver hinged double-jaw tip with horizontal serrations, teeth, or fenestrations (window openings in the blades). Exhibits high-contrast linear specular reflections (bright white highlights) along the metallic jaws and hinge.
structures.where_found: Enters from the periphery of the frame: typically the assistant's grasper enters from the bottom-left/far-right lateral port pushing the gallbladder fundus toward the top-left, while the surgeon's left-hand grasper enters from the left/epigastric region retracting Hartmann's pouch inferolaterally toward the bottom-left.
structures.when_visible: Visible across Phases 1 to 7; usually 1 or 2 graspers are visible simultaneously holding or retracting the gallbladder wall or adjacent tissue.
structures.how_to_tell_apart: Mark POSITIVE only if the instrument has a hinged two-jaw gripping tip (open or closed on tissue) with serrated/fenestrated metallic blades or a clearly identifiable grasper shaft attached to gripping jaws. Do NOT label `l_hook` (which has a single thin 90-degree bent wire tip and no hinge), clip appliers (wider 10 mm blocky grooved distal housing holding a clip), or scissors (overlapping bevelled shearing blades).

structures.name: L-Hook Electrocautery
structures.appearance: Elongated cylindrical shaft covered in matte black, grey, yellow, or blue insulation, terminating in a thin, bare, single-piece metallic silver wire bent at a 90-degree right angle (L-shape). Produces bright point/linear specular highlights on the metal hook and, when activated, emits bright yellow/white electrical arcs, surgical smoke plumes, and leaves charred black/white desiccated tissue.
structures.where_found: Enters from the surgeon's right-hand working port (epigastric), typically projecting into the frame from the right or top-right border toward the central dissection plane (Calot's triangle or the cystic plate/liver bed).
structures.when_visible: Visible primarily in Phase 2 (Calot's triangle dissection) and Phase 4 (gallbladder dissection off the liver bed), and occasionally Phase 6 (spot coagulation of the liver bed).
structures.how_to_tell_apart: Mark POSITIVE when the insulated shaft terminates in a narrow, single-piece L-shaped right-angle metallic wire hook (even if the hook tip is partially buried in tissue during cautery, provided the characteristic narrow collar and L-bend or cautery action are clear). Do NOT label hinged two-jaw instruments (`grasper`), flat paddle-shaped spatula cautery, or wide hollow suction tubes with lateral holes.

structures.name: Liver
structures.appearance: Large, voluminous, solid parenchymal organ. Healthy liver is deep reddish-brown to dark mahogany with a smooth, wet, glistening capsule (Glisson's capsule) producing high-contrast specular reflections. Steatotic liver appears yellowish-tan with rounded edges; cirrhotic liver appears nodular. In Phase 4–6, the exposed cystic plate (liver bed) on its undersurface appears pale whitish-pink (fibrous layer) or charred brown/black from electrocautery.
structures.where_found: Dominates the superior, upper-left, and upper-right quadrants of the video frame (Segments IVb and V), arching over the gallbladder fossa and forming the superior boundary of the hepatocystic triangle.
structures.when_visible: Visible throughout Phases 1 to 7, typically occupying 25% to 35% of the frame, including both the intact capsular surface and the raw/cauterized hepatic bed.
structures.how_to_tell_apart: Mark POSITIVE for the solid reddish-brown organ parenchyma, its sharp/rounded inferior border, and its attached cystic plate bed. Distinguish from `blood` and hematoma: `liver` has a firm, structured contour, smooth glistening Glisson's capsule with organized subcapsular vascular patterns, and retains its shape, whereas `blood` is a formless, gravity-dependent dark/crimson liquid or jelly-like clot coating tissue planes. Distinguish from the diaphragm/abdominal wall superiorly by the paler pink striated muscle fibers and the dividing white falciform ligament.

structures.name: Gallbladder
structures.appearance: Elongated, distended, pear-shaped hollow saccular viscus. Healthy serosa is smooth, glossy, translucent robin's-egg blue, greenish-grey, or pale whitish-yellow. In chronic cholecystitis or omental adhesions, it appears thick, opaque milky-white, or covered in yellow pericholecystic fat; in acute inflammation, it is tense, edematous, and beefy-red/violaceous.
structures.where_found: Positioned centrally and upper-centrally, tucked directly beneath the inferior border of the liver (between Segments IVb and V). Under grasper traction, it stretches longitudinally from the top-left (fundus) down to the center-bottom (infundibulum/Hartmann's pouch).
structures.when_visible: Visible in Phases 1 to 5 (from initial retraction through Calot's dissection, clipping/cutting, liver bed detachment, and placement into the retrieval bag).
structures.how_to_tell_apart: Mark POSITIVE for the bulbous fundus, body, and tapering infundibulum (Hartmann's pouch) attached to the liver bed or held by graspers. Do NOT include the narrowed tubular `cystic_duct` below the infundibular neck inside the `gallbladder` box. Distinguish from bowel (duodenum/colon at bottom-right), which has pinkish-tan smooth muscle serosa, haustra, and peristalsis, and from flat white fibrous liver ligaments attached to the anterior abdominal wall.

structures.name: Cystic Duct
structures.appearance: Short (2–4 cm), narrow (2–3 mm diameter), distinct cylindrical tubular conduit. Appears pale pinkish-white, greyish, or slightly yellowish-green, with a firm, slightly beaded or spiral contour (from internal spiral valves of Heister) and no pulsation. In Phase 3, it may have shiny metallic titanium or polymer clips clamped across its lumen.
structures.where_found: Located in the lower-central surgical field within Calot's (hepatocystic) triangle, running directly from the tapering neck/infundibulum of the gallbladder inferomedially toward the hepatoduodenal ligament/common bile duct.
structures.when_visible: Visible ONLY in Phase 2 (after the visceral peritoneum and surrounding adipose/fibrofatty tissue in Calot's triangle have been dissected and cleared to skeletonize the duct) and Phase 3 (during clipping and division, and as a clipped ductal stump).
confused_with: Common bile duct (CBD) / common hepatic duct (CHD)
Fibrous connective tissue or peritoneal strands
structures.how_to_tell_apart: Mark POSITIVE ONLY when a skeletonized, distinct cylindrical tubular structure is visibly isolated and continuous with the gallbladder infundibulum (including its clipped stump). Mark ABSENT (0) in early Phase 1/2 when the hepatocystic triangle is still covered by intact peritoneum and yellow fat. Distinguish from the cystic artery (which runs superior/deep to the duct, is narrower, pinkish-red, smoother without beaded contours, and branches onto the gallbladder wall), from cobweb-like translucent fibrous strands (which lack a true cylindrical wall/lumen), and from the wider (>4–6 mm) CBD running vertically deeper in the hepatoduodenal ligament.

structures.name: Free Blood or Blood Clot
structures.appearance: High-contrast bright crimson/red liquid when fresh and oxygenated, or dark maroon to brownish-black when venous, pooled, or coagulated. Appears as a free-flowing gravity-dependent liquid trickle/stream, a dark glistening pool in dependent recesses, or a glossy wet red staining layer actively coating fat and dissected connective tissue planes.
structures.where_found: Typically found trickling down the dissected cystic plate (liver bed), oozing around vascular/ductal stumps in Calot's triangle, or pooling in dependent recesses at the bottom/bottom-left of the frame (Morrison's pouch / hepatorenal recess).
structures.when_visible: Variable, occurring primarily during Phases 2, 4, and 6 when tissue dissection breaches vessels or the cystic plate prior to suctioning/irrigation and coagulation.
confused_with: Pink/reddish hyperemic serosa or inflamed tissue
Intact blood vessels (cystic artery, hepatic vein tributaries)
Dry black/brown electrocautery char or golden-green bile
structures.how_to_tell_apart: Mark POSITIVE ONLY when distinct extravasated free liquid red blood, active trickling/oozing, or dark jelly-like pooled blood clots are visible outside of vessels. Do NOT label normal dark reddish-brown `liver` parenchyma, pink/reddish vascularized serosa/fat, intact bluish/red blood vessels confined within a tubular wall, golden-brown/greenish bile leaks, or dry black/brown electrocautery eschar/char on the liver bed.

critical_events: Achievement of the Critical View of Safety (CVS) at the end of Phase 2 prior to clipping: (1) hepatocystic triangle completely cleared of fat and fibrous tissue so background liver (Segment V) is visible through the window, (2) lower one-third of the gallbladder dissected free from the fibrous cystic plate, and (3) two and only two tubular structures (cystic duct and cystic artery) seen entering the gallbladder directly.

Maintenance of dissection ventral/superior to Rouviere's sulcus and the R4U line (from the roof of Rouviere's sulcus across the base of Segment IV) to prevent common bile duct (CBD) and right hepatic artery injury.

Avoidance of the Infundibular ('Tunnel') Trap in severe inflammation/Mirizzi syndrome where excessive cephalad traction aligns the CBD with the cystic duct, causing dissection behind the CBD and misidentification of the CBD as the cystic duct.

Breaching the fibrous cystic plate into deep liver parenchyma during Phase 4 dissection, which exposes middle hepatic vein tributaries and causes brisk venous hemorrhage (`blood` surge) obscuring the field.

Thermal and clipping hazards: activating `l_hook` within <5 mm of metallic clips or the CBD (risking thermal necrosis and bile leak) or applying clips that fail to fully span the diameter of a dilated `cystic_duct`.
general_rules: SINGLE-FRAME EVIDENCE ONLY: Base all presence/absence (0/1) decisions and 2D bounding boxes strictly on visual features present in the current static frame, without assuming an object is present just because of the surgical phase.

PERIPHERY AND EDGE SCANNING: Systematically inspect all four borders and corners of the circular/rectangular endoscopic viewport before finalizing labels; `grasper` tips/shafts, `l_hook` shafts, and the `liver` edge frequently appear partially cropped or darkened by vignetting at the frame periphery and must be labeled if identifiable.

INSTRUMENT DIFFERENTIATION (`grasper` vs `l_hook`): Inspect the distal working tip carefully—label `grasper` only when hinged double jaws (serrated, toothed, or fenestrated, whether open or clamped on tissue) or a known grasper shaft gripping tissue is visible; label `l_hook` only when the thin, single-piece 90-degree bent metallic wire hook tip (or its distinctive narrow collar actively cauterizing tissue) is visible.

STRICT `cystic_duct` EXPOSURE RULE: Mark `cystic_duct` as present (1) ONLY when surgical dissection has stripped away the overlying peritoneum and adipose tissue to expose a distinct, cylindrical tubular duct stub directly continuous with the gallbladder infundibulum (or its clipped stump). If the region below the infundibulum is still buried in undissected yellow fat or intact peritoneal sheets, mark `cystic_duct` as absent (0).

STRICT `blood` EXTRAVASATION RULE: Mark `blood` as present (1) ONLY when free-flowing crimson liquid, active red trickling/oozing across tissue planes, or dark maroon pooled clots are visibly present outside blood vessels. Never label healthy reddish-brown `liver` parenchyma, pink hyperemic gallbladder/peritoneal serosa, intact blood vessels, or dry black/brown cautery char as `blood`.

TIGHT BOUNDING BOX GEOMETRY: Draw tight 2D bounding boxes around the visible pixel extent of each present class instance—for instruments (`grasper`, `l_hook`), include both the visible metallic working tip and the visible insulated shaft up to the frame edge; for `gallbladder` and `cystic_duct`, separate their boxes at the anatomic transition where the bulbous infundibulum (Hartmann's pouch) narrows into the cylindrical duct.
